All components (control plane serve, migrate, gateway, and the sandbox runtime factory-agent run) share the same two settings.
Variable Required Default Effect DF_LOG_FORMAT no text text: human-readable lines. json: one JSON object per line with timestamp, level, target and fields (fields.message is the message). Also available as --log-format. An unknown value makes the process exit with an error naming the variable. RUST_LOG no info Log level in EnvFilter syntax (info, debug, info,df_web=debug). Unset, empty or invalid values log at info; an invalid value also logs a warning naming RUST_LOG. Clap usage errors are printed to stderr as plain text in both formats.
data.per-component-levels#Per-component level: Component Level source Control plane, migrate RUST_LOG (Helm: controlPlane.logLevel) Gateway RUST_LOG (Helm: gateway.logLevel) Sandbox runtime instance config sandbox.logLevel (default info), set by the control plane as the sandbox’s RUST_LOG The control plane sets DF_LOG_FORMAT in every sandbox to its own effective format. Helm values: logging.format (all components), see deploy/helm/dark-factory/README.md.
data.sandbox-session-events#Sandbox session e:
factory-agent logs the session at INFO so a run can be followed from the pod log: run assigned, harness started, harness session ready, prompt received, turn started, user message delivered, tool call (title, kind, origin, input), tool call status changed, plan updated, turn ended, notices (WARN for warning and error notices), push reports and the run report.
input is the tool’s raw input cut to 512 bytes (input_truncated=true when cut). Operators who cannot accept tool input in logs set sandbox.logLevel: warn. Agent message and thought chunks are logged at DEBUG only. Tool output, tool content, prompt content and credentials are never logged.

data:
The control plane (dark-factory serve) and the gateway (dark-factory gateway) export OpenTelemetry metrics and, optionally, traces. migrate and the sandbox runtime export nothing: the runtime sends its measurements to the control plane over the agent channel (RuntimeTiming), and the control plane derives the run metrics from the messages it persists.
flowchart LR runtime[Sandbox runtime] -- "agent messages incl. RuntimeTiming (mTLS, durable outbox)" --> cp[Control plane] cp -- "after commit" --> meters[OTel meter provider] gw[Gateway] --> meters meters -- "GET /metrics :9464" --> prom[Prometheus] meters -- "OTLP/gRPC push" --> coll[OTel Collector]
data.configuration#Configuration:
Standard OTEL_* variables; Helm renders them from telemetry.* (see deploy/helm/dark-factory/README.md).
Variable Required Default Effect OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER no prometheus Comma-separated list of prometheus, otlp, none. none alone disables metrics. An unknown value stops the process at startup, the error names the variable. OTEL_EXPORTER_PROMETHEUS_HOST no 0.0.0.0 Address of the scrape endpoint. OTEL_EXPORTER_PROMETHEUS_PORT no 9464 Port of GET /metrics, separate from all other listeners. OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER no none otlp exports spans; none installs no exporter and opens no connection. OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG no parentbased_always_on always_on, always_off, traceidratio (argument: ratio from 0 to 1, default 1), each also with the prefix parentbased_. Other values stop the process at startup. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, _HEADERS, _INSECURE, _TIMEOUT with otlp none OTLP over gRPC. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL (also _METRICS_PROTOCOL, _TRACES_PROTOCOL) accepts only grpc; any other value stops the process at startup. An endpoint without scheme uses https; the native root store and a mounted private CA are honoured. OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL no 60000 (ms) Push interval of the otlp metrics exporter. OTEL_SERVICE_NAME no dark-factory-control-plane / dark-factory-gateway service.name. OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES no none Extra resource attributes. Every metric and span carries the resource attributes service.name, service.version and service.instance.id (pod name, else host name). service.version is the release version the binary was built with, dev for unstamped builds. Build-time variable DF_VERSION (optional, default dev; an empty value also gives dev): Bazel sets it from --//build:version=, plain cargo with DF_VERSION= cargo build. OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.version=… overrides it.
Export failures never affect the component; the SDK logs them at ERROR once per export interval. On shutdown pending exports are flushed within the shutdown grace period (30 s) counted from the signal: what the listeners did not use is left for the flush.
data.control-plane#Control plane:
Instrument Type Unit Attributes Source df.runs.ended counter project, outcome RunReport df.run.duration histogram s project, outcome run start to RunReport df.agent.turns counter project, stop_reason TurnEnded df.agent.tokens counter model, token_type (input, output, cache_read, cache_write) stored gateway usage records (a record that is stored twice counts once) df.agent.tool_calls counter project, kind, origin, status (completed, failed) terminal status of a tool call df.agent.pushes counter project, target, status PushReport df.agent.runtime.duration histogram s project, operation, result (ok, error) RuntimeTiming df.agent.runtime.rejected counter project, operation RuntimeTiming with a duration of zero or more than 7 days df.agent.connections up-down counter project open agent channel streams df.agent.reconnects counter project streams of runs that had one before df.outbox.jobs counter kind (pr.mark_draft, pr.sync, lifecycle_event.deliver), result (done, retry, gave_up) every outbox job attempt, on the leader df.lifecycle_event.deliveries counter result (delivered, failed, refused) every lifecycle event delivery attempt; given-up deliveries are counted by df.outbox.jobs{kind="lifecycle_event.deliver",result="gave_up"} df.webhook.requests counter plugin, outcome (accepted, unauthorized, not_found, too_large, invalid, error) every request to POST /webhooks/{plugin}; Prometheus: df_webhook_requests_total operation is one of workspace_prepare, harness_start, turn, push, finalize. outcome, stop_reason, kind, origin, target and status are the lower-case protobuf enum names without prefix (end_turn, task_branch); unknown numbers are unspecified. The kind of df.outbox.jobs is the outbox job kind instead. refused means the project subscription’s host is not a public address. plugin of df.webhook.requests is the plugin name under plugins for a loaded plugin, or unknown for any other name.
Attributes that originate from the sandbox are bounded: model is cut to 64 bytes and after 32 distinct values per process further ones are other. Run ids, task keys, tool titles, repository URLs and hosts are never attributes.
data.gateway#Gateway: Instrument Type Unit Attributes Meaning df.gateway.connections counter decision (allowed, denied), reason (deny reason or none) proxy requests by final decision, counted when they end df.gateway.active_connections up-down counter requests connected to their destination df.gateway.bytes counter By direction (upstream: sandbox to destination, downstream) relayed bytes df.gateway.policy_version gauge version of the last applied allowlist snapshot df.gateway.inference.requests counter wire_api (anthropic-messages, openai-chat, openai-responses), status_class (2xx, 4xx, 5xx, error) model requests of the inference endpoint, counted when their response ends df.gateway.inference.duration histogram s wire_api time from the request to the end of its response df.gateway.inference.usage_dropped counter usage records dropped because the buffer was full or the control plane refused them
data.how-to-enable-tracing#How to enable trac:
Run an OTLP/gRPC collector that Jaeger, Tempo or similar reads from.
Set the endpoint and enable traces, in Helm:
telemetry: traces: enabled: true sampler: parentbased_traceidratio samplerArg: '0.1' otlp: endpoint: https://otel-collector.observability.svc:4317 or as variables: OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=....
Look for service.name dark-factory-control-plane and dark-factory-gateway.
Spans pass the same RUST_LOG filter as log events: RUST_LOG=info exports the INFO spans listed above.
data.instruments#Instruments: Recording is best-effort: the control plane records after the transaction that persists a message committed, never for replayed messages, so a crash between commit and recording loses the sample. Run instruments carry project (project key). Prometheus renders df.agent.turns as df_agent_turns_total and appends the unit (df_run_duration_seconds).
data.spans#Spans:
Only with OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp. Attributes never contain credentials, prompts or tool input/output.
Span Attributes http.request http.request.method, http.route, http.response.status_code (UI and gateway health listeners; the /metrics scrape endpoint gets no span) agent.session run_id agent.persist_batch messages (count) gateway.connect method, decision, host (allowed requests only) Spans of the runtime and trace context propagation over the agent channel are not part of this.

data: Upgrades: moving to a new release and what cannot be rolled back. Backup and restore: what holds state and how to save it. Troubleshooting: runs that do not start or end unexpectedly. Several instances in one cluster: production and dev side by side.

All state of an instance is in its PostgreSQL database: projects, personas, credential references, tasks, runs, transcripts (binary content included), requests, egress rules, push records and the audit log. Back up the database; everything else can be recreated.
What Where Back up? Database PostgreSQL, schema dark_factory yes Code the forge: task branches factory/task/ and WIP snapshots factory/wip/ by the forge’s own backup Secret values (forge and harness tokens, database passwords, OIDC client secret) Kubernetes Secrets in the instance namespace yes, with your usual Secret handling; the database only holds references Task volumes PVCs in the sandbox namespace no: a cache; the next run re-clones from the task branch and the WIP snapshot Live traffic events gateway memory no: ephemeral by design Helm values your values.yaml keep it in version control
data.back-up#Back up:
Any PostgreSQL backup method works (pg_dump, your operator’s scheduled backups, volume snapshots of the database server). A logical dump of the instance’s database:
pg_dump --format=custom --file=dark-factory-$(date +%F).dump \ "postgresql://dark_factory_owner@postgres.databases.svc/dark_factory" Take one before every upgrade: schema migrations cannot be undone (Upgrades).
data.restore#Restore: Scale the control plane to zero, so nothing writes during the restore: kubectl -n dark-factory scale deploy/dark-factory-control-plane --replicas=0. Restore into an empty database owned by the owner role, for example pg_restore --no-owner --role=dark_factory_owner --dbname=dark_factory dark-factory-2026-11-04.dump. Run helm upgrade with the release that matches the backup. The migrate job re-applies the application role’s grants. Scale the control plane back up. Runs that were active when the backup was taken have no sandbox anymore; they end as sandbox_lost and their tasks are queued again.

data: Two or more Dark Factory instances can run in one cluster, for example a production and a dev instance. Each instance is its own Helm release in its own namespace. The release name may be the same.
data.example-production-and-dev#Example: prod:
values-dev.yaml, next to the production values:
database: host: postgres.databases.svc database: dark_factory_dev oidc: issuerUrl: https://id.example.org/realms/dark-factory-dev publicUrl: https://factory-dev.example.org sandboxNamespace: name: dark-factory-dev-sandboxes httpRoute: enabled: true parentRefs: - name: public namespace: gateway-system hostnames: - factory-dev.example.org helm install dark-factory oci://ghcr.io/prskr/dark-factory/charts/dark-factory \ --namespace dark-factory-dev --create-namespace \ --version 2026.11.1 \ --values values-dev.yaml Check that the cluster-scoped roles of both instances exist side by side:
kubectl get clusterroles -l app.kubernetes.io/name=dark-factory
data.what-each-instance-needs-of-its-own#What: Item Value Why Release namespace --namespace The chart names its cluster-scoped objects after it. Sandbox namespace sandboxNamespace.name A shared sandbox namespace collides on the namespace and its policies, and each control plane would see the other’s sandboxes. The chart cannot detect it. Database database.host, database.database Each instance migrates and owns its schema. URL and OIDC client oidc.publicUrl, oidc.*, httpRoute.hostnames Logins and redirects go to one instance. Cluster-scoped objects (RBAC for reading the sandbox namespace and cluster targets, the CA issuer) and the reader roles in shared clusterTargets.namespaces carry the release namespace in their names, so the releases do not collide on them. Names stay within 63 characters; the chart README lists them.

data: The task’s details show the outcome of each run; the control plane log has the reason (see Logging).
data.a-run-cannot-do-its-work#A run cannot do: Symptom Cause and fix A network-access request for a host The host has no allow rule: approve the request or add a rule (Network access). Git clone or push fails with 403 The gateway does not know the pod yet (retried), or the path names another task. Git fails with 502 The forge rejected the project’s forge credential: check the token and its scopes (Forges). git push prints df:… A push check rejected it; in approval mode a push-check-exception request appears in the inbox (Git proxy). The harness gets 404 from the gateway The path is not one of the inference endpoint’s, or the provider does not offer that wire API. The task becomes rate_limited The model provider’s usage limit; the task resumes at the shown time. No pull request appears The task branch has no commit ahead of the base branch yet, or the forge plugin failed. Pull request actions are outbox jobs, retried with backoff (30 s doubling to 10 min) for an hour, also across control plane restarts; see df.outbox.jobs{kind="pr.sync"} and the control plane log. After the hour the next push ahead of the base branch or run end that pushed opens it. A run that never pushed the task branch opens none. Pull request stays a draft after completion Same cause: marking it ready failed and is retried for an hour (df.outbox.jobs{kind="pr.sync"}, control plane log). A new message after the completion keeps the pull request a draft on purpose. After the hour, the next completed run or Mark done marks it ready.
data.a-task-does-not-start#A task does not st: Symptom Cause and fix The task stays queued All run slots are busy (runs.maxConcurrent, default 4), or its resume time lies ahead (shown in the details). The run stays provisioning A cluster service rule of the run cannot be resolved right now, and the control plane has no earlier resolution of it. Transient causes: a timeout, a 5xx, 408 or 429 from the Kubernetes API, a connection error, or a named targetPort that no selected pod exposes (no EndpointSlice port named after the Service port). It creates no pod; every attempt logs a warning whose error contains cluster target(s) temporarily unresolvable: / (the first attempt as sandbox provider temporarily unavailable, run stays provisioning, retries as provisioning a stale run again failed; retrying on a later tick). Once the run is a minute old it retries every 5 s. Check the Service, its endpoints and the API server; for a named targetPort, check the Service’s selector and the pods’ named container ports. If the target never resolves, the run ends connect_timeout after runs.connectTimeoutSeconds. The run ends provisioning_failed The sandbox pod or the task volume could not be created: check the events in the sandbox namespace (kubectl -n dark-factory-sandboxes get events), the ResourceQuota, the storage class and the project’s sandbox image. A retry of a stale run also ends this way if the quota or the sandbox spec rejects it. The task is queued again automatically, up to runs.maxAutoResumes times (default 3, 0 disables it, see Agent runs); then it becomes failed: fix the cause and send the task a new message. A quota rejection does not count towards the limit. The run ends connect_timeout The runtime did not reach the control plane within runs.connectTimeoutSeconds (600 s). If no sandbox pod was created, see the row “The run stays provisioning” above. If the pod exists, check its log, the certificate from cert-manager’s CSI driver, and the NetworkPolicy from the sandbox namespace to the control plane’s agent port. Queued again automatically up to runs.maxAutoResumes times, like provisioning_failed. The run ends sandbox_lost The pod disappeared: deleted, evicted, out of memory, or an image could not be pulled. Queued again automatically up to runs.maxAutoResumes times, like provisioning_failed. The run’s detail names the cause (below). Detail sandbox is gone: image pull failed: : , sandbox is gone: ErrImagePull: or sandbox is gone: ImagePullBackOff: The kubelet could not pull an image of the sandbox pod: the runtime image, the harness image or the project’s sandbox image (the message names it). Check the image reference and tag, the registry’s reachability from the node and its credentials. Detail sandbox pod no longer present after a control plane restart The pod was deleted while no control plane replica ran. The next control plane start ends such runs. If the Kubernetes API fails, the check is retried twice, 5 s apart; the log then shows gave up checking runs for lost sandboxes after a restart, and runs left unchecked end on their timeouts. The harness answers with an error about the model The gateway could not use the persona’s model provider: 502 means the provider’s Secret is unreadable or the upstream is unreachable.
data.login-problems#Login problems: See the troubleshooting tables of Keycloak and Dex.

data: Dark Factory is pre-MVP: any release may change the configuration, the database schema or the web UI incompatibly, and there are no migration guarantees between releases yet. Read the release notes on the releases page before every upgrade.
data.cluster-scoped-rbac-names#Cluster-scoped:
The cluster-scoped ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings and the reader Roles in clusterTargets.namespaces now carry the release namespace in their names (--…), so that several instances can share a cluster. helm upgrade removes the old objects and creates the new ones; no step is needed.
If - is longer than 40 characters, it is now shortened with a hash instead of being cut off, which also renames the chart-created CA (tls.ca.create: true). cert-manager then issues new certificates from a new CA: let active runs finish before the upgrade, since sandboxes with a certificate of the old CA lose their connection.
data.model-providers-inference-endpoint#Model:
From this release on, harnesses reach their model through the gateway’s inference endpoint, and every persona uses a model provider instead of a harness credential. No model credential reaches a sandbox any more.
The migrate job converts the data: for every credential that personas used as harness credential, it creates one model provider “Claude subscription ()” (Anthropic Messages, https://api.anthropic.com, scheme claude-subscription) and points those personas at it.
A persona without a harness credential stops the migration with a message naming the persona. The migrate job fails and the release stays on the old version. Give the persona a harness credential (or delete it), then upgrade again.
After the upgrade, check Settings → Model providers and the persona list; add providers for other services as needed. A persona created later needs a model provider.
Remove api.anthropic.com from the instance egress allowlist: model traffic no longer uses the egress proxy. Leaving the entry is harmless.
Run the gateway and the control plane from the same chart version: the gateway reports usage over a new internal call.
The Helm value and instance setting forge.allowPlainHttp moved to network.allowPlainHttp, because it now also governs the model provider upstreams. There is no alias: rename it in your values.yaml (or in the network section of a hand-written instance config). The old key is ignored silently, and plain HTTP stays off until you do.
To roll back, restore the database backup taken before the upgrade, then roll back the release (see above): the migration cannot be reverted.
data.other-releases#Other releases: Some releases need a step beyond helm upgrade, for example removing the forge host from the egress rules after the switch to the Git proxy. They are listed in the release notes and in the chart README.
data.prompt-batches#Prompt batches:
The agent protocol replaces the singular Prompt control message with Prompts batches. The sandbox runtime and control plane must come from the same release and chart version. If you pin their images, align both pins with that version.
Let active runs finish before upgrading, or accept the interrupted-run behavior described above. Roll back the runtime and control plane together, following the database restore requirements.
data.provider-models-and-the-opencode-harness:
Personas now select a model of their model provider, and the harness opencode is available (guide).
The migrate job turns the model of every persona into a model of its provider on Anthropic Messages, without limits, and the persona references it. The Anthropic Messages API must be one of the provider’s (the providers the previous migration created are). A persona without a model stops the migration with a message naming the persona. The migrate job fails and the release stays on the old version. Set a model on the persona (or delete it), then upgrade again. The model is required from now on. After the upgrade, add the models you use on the provider’s Models tab (the presets prefill them) before you create personas on a new provider; a persona can only select a model the provider lists. The agent protocol changed: the runtime writes the files of Assign.harness.acp.files instead of fixed Claude Code paths. Run the sandbox runtime and the control plane from the same chart version; let active runs finish before the upgrade. A new image opencode-harness and the values image.harness.opencode.* (instance setting harness.opencode.image) hold OpenCode. The chart default tag is the OpenCode version; released charts pin the image digest. The claude-harness image has no launcher any more: the default harness.claudeCode.adapterCommand is ["/opt/harness/claude-code/bin/node", "/opt/harness/claude-code/node_modules/@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp/dist/index.js"] (it was ["/opt/harness/claude-code/bin/claude-agent-acp"]). If you override the setting, change it to the new command, otherwise claude-code runs fail to start. Use the chart version for the control plane and the harness image together. To roll back, restore the database backup taken before the upgrade, then roll back the release.
data.rolling-back#Rolling back: Schema migrations only go forward: there are no down migrations. helm rollback restores the old images and values but not the old schema, and an older control plane may not start on a newer schema. To go back, restore the database backup taken before the upgrade, then roll back the release.
data.upgrade-a-release#Upgrade a release:
Back up the database (Backup and restore).
Let active runs finish, or accept that they are cut off: a run whose sandbox disappears ends with sandbox_lost and its task is queued again automatically.
Upgrade with the new chart version and your values:
helm upgrade dark-factory oci://ghcr.io/prskr/dark-factory/charts/dark-factory \ --namespace dark-factory \ --version 2026.11.1 \ --values values.yaml The migrate job runs first (pre-upgrade hook) and applies the new schema migrations; then the control plane and the gateway roll. Check:
kubectl -n dark-factory get pods kubectl -n dark-factory rollout status deploy/dark-factory-control-plane The profile menu shows the new version and links to its docs.
The control plane, runtime, gateway and plugin images follow the chart’s appVersion unless you pinned them; a pinned plugin image keeps its version until you change it.

data:
Configuration references of the components:
Sandbox runtime: environment variables of factory-agent run. Agent channel: the connection between the sandbox runtime and the control plane. Plugins: forge plugins, their routing and settings.
dark-factory serve starts the agent port and the run scheduler. Settings come from the instance configuration file (--config, default /etc/dark-factory/config.yaml).
data.configuration#Configuration: Key Required Default Effect server.agentPort no 9443 Port of the mTLS agent service, separate from server.httpPort. agent.tls.certFile yes none PEM server certificate (chain) of the agent port. serve refuses to start without agent.tls. The three files are checked for changes at most every 10 s; changed (rotated) material applies to new connections without a restart, material that does not parse is ignored with a warning. agent.tls.keyFile yes none PEM private key of certFile. agent.tls.clientCaFile yes none PEM CA bundle. Client certificates must chain to it. agent.commitIdentity.name / .email no Dark Factory / dark-factory@localhost Commit identity in Assign.workspace.commit_identity. agent.gitUsername no dark-factory User name the gateway’s Git proxy sends with the project’s forge token. harness.claudeCode.image no ghcr.io/prskr/dark-factory/claude-harness:0.95.0 Harness image, mounted read-only at /opt/harness/claude-code in the sandbox of every run whose project has no adapter command. The tag is the adapter version. The chart renders it from image.harness.claudeCode.*. harness.claudeCode.adapterCommand no ["/opt/harness/claude-code/bin/node", "/opt/harness/claude-code/node_modules/@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp/dist/index.js"] ACP adapter command from the harness image; a project’s own adapter command replaces it (and the harness image mount). Personas have no adapter command. harness.claudeCode.env no {} Non-secret environment for the harness (Assign.harness.acp.env). harness.claudeCode.settingsJson no "" Claude Code settings.json content. A non-empty value is passed as the harness file .claude/settings.json (Assign.harness.acp.files), which the runtime writes before every start. harness.opencode.image no ghcr.io/prskr/dark-factory/opencode-harness:2.2.5 Image of the opencode harness (patched OpenCode release binary and the musl runtime it needs), mounted read-only at /opt/harness/opencode in the sandbox of every opencode run whose project has no adapter command. The tag is the OpenCode version. The chart renders it from image.harness.opencode.*. A blank value counts as not configured: such a run fails provisioning with a message naming the harness. harness.opencode.adapterCommand no ["/opt/harness/opencode/bin/opencode", "acp"] ACP adapter command from the harness image; a project’s own adapter command replaces it (and the harness image mount). harness.opencode.env no {} Non-secret environment for the harness (Assign.harness.acp.env). The environment below wins over it. runs.maxWallClockSeconds no 7200 Assign.budgets.max_wall_clock. Counts from the runtime’s first Hello, not from run creation. A value too large to represent as a date means no limit. runs.connectTimeoutSeconds no 600 Time from run creation until the runtime opens its stream; then the run fails with connect_timeout. runs.cancelGraceSeconds no 300 Grace after the wall-clock budget. runs.keepAliveSeconds no 600 How long a run waits for a follow-up after a normal turn end (awaiting_input) before the control plane sends Release and the run ends end_turn. 0 releases right after the turn. Idle time counts toward maxWallClockSeconds. volumes.retainAfterCloseSeconds no 604800 (7 days) The volume of a completed or cancelled task without an active run is deleted this long after its last run ended. The volume of a task whose pull request was merged is deleted at the next check, whatever this value. The check runs once per hour on the replica holding the instance Lease (not without a cluster). 0 deletes at the next check; a value too large to represent as a date means never. volumes.idleTtlSeconds no 2592000 (30 days) The volume of any task without an active run is deleted this long after its last run ended; same check and value rules as retainAfterCloseSeconds. The next run creates a fresh volume, clones again and restores the WIP snapshot. A board member can delete a volume at once with “Reset workspace” (crates/df-web/README.md). runs.maxConcurrent no 4 At least 1 (0 is rejected at startup). Runs that may be non-terminal at the same time, counted across all replicas. Further due tasks keep their status until a slot frees and then start oldest resume time first. runs.maxAutoResumes no 3 Consecutive automatic resumes after sandbox_lost, connect_timeout or provisioning_failed (backoff 2 min x (resumes + 1)); then the task becomes failed. A message or a run that ends with a RunReport resets the count; a capacity rejection does not count. artifacts.maxTextBytes no 1048576 (1 MiB) Largest text artifact (write_artifact). Between 1 and 8388608 (8 MiB, the most the runtime sends); anything else is rejected at startup. artifacts.maxImageBytes no 3932160 (3.75 MiB) Largest image artifact (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF), also limited to 8000 px per side (a constant). Same range as maxTextBytes. artifacts.maxPerTask no 50 Artifacts per task, at least 1. Replacing an artifact does not count; a write of a new name over the limit is rejected. web.showHiddenBlocks no false Show transcript content blocks marked hidden (instructions for the agent, e.g. the set_task_title request) in the task page and the queued message stack, muted and labeled “Instruction for the agent”. Hidden blocks are always delivered to the harness. Read at startup; a change needs a restart. web.codeTheme.light no InspiredGitHub Theme of highlighted code blocks in agent messages in the light UI theme. One of InspiredGitHub, Solarized (light), Solarized (dark), base16-ocean.light, base16-ocean.dark, base16-eighties.dark, base16-mocha.dark. An unknown name fails startup with an error that names the option and lists the valid themes. Read at startup; a change needs a restart. web.codeTheme.dark no base16-ocean.dark Theme of highlighted code blocks in the dark UI theme; same names and rules as web.codeTheme.light. lifecycleEvents.signingKeyFile no none PEM file with the instance’s Ed25519 private key (PKCS#8, as written by cert-manager or openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519). Unset, lifecycle events are off: nothing is recorded or sent, and GET /lifecycle-events/public-key answers 404. Set, serve refuses to start if the file cannot be read or holds no Ed25519 key; the public key is served at GET /lifecycle-events/public-key (whpk_, no login). Read at startup. lifecycleEvents.subscriptions[].url no [] Instance subscription: receives the events of every project. Must be an http(s) URL; any address is allowed, including cluster-internal ones. Subscriptions without signingKeyFile refuse the start. lifecycleEvents.subscriptions[].events no [] (all) Event types sent to this subscription (volume.provisioned, volume.destroyed, sandbox.provisioning, sandbox.provisioned, sandbox.provisioning_failed, sandbox.destroyed). Empty means all, including types added later. An unknown type refuses the start. The Helm chart sets agent.tls to the cert-manager secret mounted at /etc/dark-factory/tls.
data.database-changes#Database changes:
20261105000004_task_dependencies.sql adds tasks.parent_id, turns tasks.created_by into a JSONB principal (existing users become human, NULL becomes system with reason migration), adds tasks.first_completed_at and tasks.first_done_at (filled from the status of existing tasks), the table task_dependencies (task_id, depends_on_task_id, kind), the status awaiting_dependencies and personas.description (at most 500 characters).
20261019000001_task_completion_summary.sql adds tasks.completion_summary (unused since 20261105000002_run_completion_summary.sql) and runs.connected_at (first Hello; start of the wall-clock budget). 20261105000002_run_completion_summary.sql adds runs.completion_summary (summary passed to complete_task by that run, posted on the pull request when the run completes; values of tasks.completion_summary are not copied). 20261105000003_task_message_queued_at_clock.sql makes task_messages.queued_at default to clock_timestamp() instead of the transaction start. The insert runs after the task row lock. The ready time of a run end or Mark done and runs.stop_requested_at are read from the same clock under that lock. Their order therefore matches the lock order, and “queued after the stop” or “queued after the completion” is exact.
data.harness-environment-and-files#Harness en:
The control plane builds Assign.harness.acp per run from the persona’s harness and the persona’s model. The wire API is the one of the model; the harness has no order of preference. Configured harness..env entries are added first, so the values below win.
claude-code opencode Wire APIs the harness can use Anthropic Messages OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages Base URL ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = /inference none; in the configuration document Persona’s model ANTHROPIC_MODEL = the model ID (ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL stays unset) none; model and small_model in the configuration document Placeholder key df-placeholder CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (provider scheme claude-subscription), otherwise ANTHROPIC_API_KEY none; in the configuration document CA file /run/factory/tls/ca.crt NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS Fixed variables CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1; CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE=/opt/harness/claude-code/bin/claude only when the run mounts the harness image OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH=1, OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1 Configuration document none OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT (below) System prompt file (below HOME) .claude/CLAUDE.md .config/opencode/AGENTS.md Other files .claude/settings.json when harness.claudeCode.settingsJson is not empty none The file list of Assign.harness.acp.files holds the system prompt (when the persona has one) and the other files of the table. The runtime writes them below /data/home and knows no harness specific path.
OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT is one JSON document per run. It ranks above OpenCode’s global and project configuration, so a repository’s opencode.json cannot redirect the model:
Part Value provider.df package by the wire API of the model (@ai-sdk/openai-compatible for Chat Completions, @ai-sdk/openai for Responses, @ai-sdk/anthropic for Messages), options.baseURL /inference/v1, options.apiKey df-placeholder provider.df.models the persona’s model; limit.context and limit.output only when the model has limits model, small_model df/ enabled_providers ["df"] autoupdate false policies denies plugin.use: plugins are neither installed nor loaded permission question and websearch denied: they are not offered to the model (questions go through the factory tool ask_question) The three files are checked for changes by the first connection that arrives at least 10 s after the last check; changed material applies to new connections without a restart, and material that does not parse is ignored (logged) until fixed. At most 256 TLS handshakes run at the same time.
data.human-stop-and-cancel#Human stop and can:
A board member stops the active run (POST /tasks/{key}/stop) or cancels the task (POST /tasks/{key}/cancel, which stops the run too). Both set runs.stop_requested_at.
A connected run in preparing, running or awaiting_input moves to finalizing; the session holding the stream sends Cancel, the runtime reports cancelled and the task becomes waiting. A run that is already finalizing is not marked by a stop (cancelling the task still marks it). A run without a connection (pending, provisioning, connecting) is ended cancelled by the scheduler on the next notification or tick and its sandbox is torn down. The task volume is kept. A stopped run that has not ended 120 s after the stop is torn down and ends cancelled with detail stop-timeout (volume kept). Task status cancelled is kept when the run ends. A message reopens the task (queued); the next run starts after the stopped run ended. Only messages queued after the stop requeue the task at run end; older undelivered messages leave it waiting. Cancelling discards the undelivered messages and closes the pending requests (task-cancelled). No pull request is opened or marked ready for a cancelled task; an existing one is left as it is.
data.idle-run-keep-alive#Idle run (keep-alive: After a normal turn end the runtime reports AWAITING_INPUT: the run becomes awaiting_input and the task waiting (it stays running while a message is undelivered). The replica holding the stream sends Release at the last persisted TurnEnded + runs.keepAliveSeconds; a replica that takes over, or a run that reconnects after the deadline, computes the same deadline. Before it sends Release (or Cancel for a task marked done) the control plane moves the run to finalizing; no prompt is sent to a finalizing run, a message queued meanwhile makes the task queued and the run end starts the next run. A message for an awaiting_input run sets the task running, starts no run and is forwarded at once.
data.protocol-behavior#Protocol behavior: Identity: the client certificate must carry the URI SAN spiffe://dark-factory/ns//pod//; SandboxProvider::resolve_identity maps SAN and peer IP to a run. Terminal runs are rejected with UNAUTHENTICATED. Handshake: Hello first (else FAILED_PRECONDITION), then HelloAck, Assign, then the prompts: undelivered prompts that are already forwarded (task_messages.forwarded_at set) are sent again, held-back ones are claimed (marked forwarded) and sent only while no turn is open (no persisted TurnStarted without a later TurnEnded). After a persisted TurnEnded the held-back prompts are sent. See “Queued messages reach the runtime between turns” in contract/README.md. Assign carries the harness environment: the gateway’s inference endpoint (https://:/inference) as base URL, the placeholder key df-placeholder and the instance CA path in the harness’s variables (Claude Code also gets CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1), from the first wire API of the harness that the persona’s model provider offers. No model credential is sent to a sandbox. Timeouts: enforce_timeouts ends every overdue run it can; a run that fails to end (or whose row cannot be read) is logged and does not stop the others. Ordering and delivery: messages are persisted in batches of up to 50 per transaction, duplicates (seq <= runs.last_persisted_seq, blobs included) are dropped, a gap closes the stream with DATA_LOSS, and the cumulative ack is sent after commit. Effects of the messages before a gap (teardown, pull request) still run. A message with an unknown body keeps its sequence number and is ignored. Tool calls and credential requests that arrive after the run ended (for example after a hard stop) are refused: an error result and DeniedReason, nothing is executed or granted. The session does not call the forge. A task-branch PushReport ahead of base (task without a pull request) and a RunReport enqueue a pr.sync outbox job in the batch transaction (payload: task_id, run_id, open, ready); a rejected non-fast-forward push sets diverged in the same transaction. A run end enqueues open if WorkspaceState.task_branch_pushed, and ready (the completion time) if the outcome is completed; a run that did neither, or a cancelled task, enqueues nothing. Mark done enqueues ready without run_id. The pr.sync handler, on every attempt: skips a missing or cancelled task; opens (or finds) the draft pull request under the per-task advisory lock task-pr: and continues with the one recorded on the task; marks it ready unless a message was queued after the ready time (checked under the same lock, which pr.mark_draft takes too); writes pr-ready: to the run’s transcript once; posts runs.completion_summary of the job’s run if non-empty. A ready-only job without a recorded pull request waits (retry) while an unfinished open job of the task exists. Forge and database errors retry with backoff (30 s base, 10 min cap, given up after 1 h; lease 3 min); an invalid payload is given up. At most 8 jobs run at once, so at most 8 pooled connections wait for or hold the advisory lock. Shutdown (SIGTERM): the scheduler lets provisioning in flight finish (10 s); sessions stop reading, finish their in-flight tool calls and credential requests (up to 20 s, then they are aborted) and end their streams; the listeners get 30 s before they are aborted. A runtime failing before Hello is logged and answered with its gRPC status. Limits: 16 MiB per message (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED above), HTTP/2 keepalive 30 s / 20 s, 10 s for the TLS handshake. Tool calls and credential requests run off the stream loop and are awaited (up to 60 s) when the stream ends. A tool call is claimed by call_id (tool_calls row) before it runs and executed at most once: a repeat gets the stored result, a call still running gets an error “in progress”, and a claim without a result after 5 minutes is closed with an error and never executed. The forge is called without an open database transaction. Executed calls are audited as tool_call.execute. Git credentials are granted only when protocol, host and path equal the project’s repository URL (a trailing .git is optional). Secret values are never logged or stored.
data.run-lifecycle#Run lifecycle:
stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> pending: task queued, no active run pending --> provisioning: volume ensured pending --> failed: provisioning_failed pending --> failed: connect_timeout provisioning --> connecting: provider Started (pod IP) provisioning --> failed: provisioning_failed provisioning --> failed: connect_timeout provisioning --> failed: sandbox_lost connecting --> preparing: Hello connecting --> failed: connect_timeout connecting --> failed: sandbox_lost preparing --> running: PhaseChanged RUNNING running --> awaiting_input: PhaseChanged AWAITING_INPUT (turn ended) awaiting_input --> running: PhaseChanged RUNNING (follow-up prompt) awaiting_input --> finalizing: idle deadline (Release) or mark done (Cancel) awaiting_input --> failed: sandbox_lost running --> finalizing: PhaseChanged FINALIZING finalizing --> succeeded: RunReport completed / end_turn / limit_reached / rate_limited finalizing --> cancelled: RunReport cancelled finalizing --> failed: RunReport failed finalizing --> failed: sandbox_lost preparing --> failed: sandbox_lost running --> failed: sandbox_lost, hard stop preparing --> finalizing: human stop (Cancel) running --> finalizing: human stop (Cancel) awaiting_input --> finalizing: human stop (Cancel) pending --> cancelled: human stop provisioning --> cancelled: human stop connecting --> cancelled: human stop finalizing --> cancelled: stop timeout (120 s) On startup the control plane ends every run in connecting or a later non-terminal state with sandbox_lost if its sandbox pod no longer exists.
A RunReport is accepted in any non-terminal state. Cancel is sent by the replica holding the stream at connect + maxWallClock + cancelGrace (and at the handshake if that moment has passed). The scheduler tears the sandbox down at connect + maxWallClock + 2 x cancelGrace. Prompts and Cancel are not sent once the run has ended; the prompt stays queued for the next run.
Run outcome Run state Task status completed succeeded in_review end_turn succeeded waiting limit_reached succeeded limit_reached cancelled cancelled waiting (cancelled if a board member cancelled the task) blocked blocked waiting rate_limited succeeded rate_limited with a resume time (the retry time, or one hour ahead) failed failed failed provisioning_failed, connect_timeout, sandbox_lost failed queued with a resume time and the resume count + 1, until runs.maxAutoResumes, then failed provisioning_failed with detail capacity (quota exceeded) failed queued in 2 minutes, resume count unchanged If prompts are still undelivered when a run ends with an outcome other than failed-class or rate_limited, the task becomes queued and the next run starts with them. A task a board member marked done, or whose pull request was merged (completed), keeps its status when its run ends, unless prompts are undelivered.
data.task-transitions-and-delegation#Task tra:
Every change of tasks.status goes through one function of df-core (task_transition::transition, ADR-0055); df_db::apply_task_event loads the task, applies the result and runs its effects in the caller’s transaction. Besides the table above:
A run that ends with completed records tasks.first_completed_at (once), releases the tasks that depend on it and wakes the parent. A task marked done records first_done_at, releases and wakes the same way; a task that ends failed or is cancelled wakes its parent. A dependent leaves awaiting_dependencies for queued when all its dependencies are satisfied (completion: first_completed_at or first_done_at is set; done: first_done_at is set). It leaves the status once. The message to the parent has the author system with reason task.child_ended and goes through the same rules as any message. No message is queued on a parent that is completed, cancelled or failed. Cross-task effects lock only the other task’s row, never its run rows. The factory tools create_task, list_personas and send_message are described in Delegate work between agents. create_task stores the title with source agent; a retried call (same call_id) returns the stored key and creates one task.

data: factory-agent run reads its configuration from environment variables. The values are read once at startup (config.rs).
data.environment-variables#Environment variab: Variable Required Default Effect DF_CONTROL_PLANE_ADDR yes none Address of the control plane gRPC endpoint. host:port is accepted; https:// is prepended when no http:// or https:// scheme is given. DF_CONTROL_PLANE_SERVER_NAME yes none TLS server name checked against the control plane certificate. DF_TLS_DIR no /run/factory/tls Directory with ca.crt (instance CA), tls.crt and tls.key (pod identity). Re-read on every connection attempt, so rotated certificates are picked up on reconnect. Git trusts ca.crt only for the gateway’s Git proxy (http..sslCAInfo: -c on the clone, then .git/config); other hosts keep the system trust store. DF_DATA_DIR no /data Persistent volume. The runtime uses repo/ (workspace checkout), home/ (harness $HOME, session logs) and runtime/ (outbox segments, run.json). DF_RUN_DIR no /run/factory Ephemeral runtime directory. Holds runtime.sock and the wip.index scratch file. Also exported to the harness. DF_RUNTIME_SOCK no /run/factory/runtime.sock Path of the runtime Unix socket. Read by the mcp subcommand (also available as --socket), which the harness starts as a child process. run creates the socket at $DF_RUN_DIR/runtime.sock and exports that path to its children. DF_LOG_FORMAT no text Log format of run: text (human-readable) or json (one JSON object per line). Also available as --log-format. Any other value makes the process exit before it starts. The control plane sets it to its own format. RUST_LOG no info Log level in EnvFilter syntax, for example info or info,factory_agent=debug. Unset, empty or invalid values log at info; an invalid value also logs a warning naming RUST_LOG. The control plane sets it from sandbox.logLevel. DEBUG adds agent message and thought chunks. A missing required variable makes run log invalid configuration and exit with status 1.
data.fixed-settings#Fixed settings:
These are compiled in and not configurable.
Setting Value Effect Agent core.hooksPath /opt/factory/hooks-empty Read-only empty hooks directory from the image. Outbox size 256 MiB, segments of 16 MiB Soft cap: senders wait when it is full; a message already taken from the queue is still stored at shutdown. Wait for Assign 10 min run exits with status 1 when the control plane sends no Assign. Handshake steps 15 s each Connect, stream open and HelloAck; then backoff and retry. Final report flush window 10 min After finalize the runtime keeps reconnecting until every outbox message, the RunReport included, is acknowledged; then it exits. If the window passes, it exits with the messages left in the outbox and the control plane later ends the run sandbox_lost and resumes the task. The window does not extend the run’s wall-clock budget. Git commands 5 min each A clone, fetch or push that takes longer is killed and fails prepare or finalize. Git retries 3, after 1 s, 5 s and 15 s Clone, fetch and push that fail transiently are retried (see “Git retries” below). Factory tool call 30 min Wait for a ToolCallResult; then the tool call returns an error. Harness exit grace 5 s Time to exit after the ACP connection closed, then it is killed.
data.other-inputs#Other inputs: Input Source Effect HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, NO_PROXY (and lowercase) environment Forwarded to git and the harness.
data.startup-and-shutdown-behavior#Startup an: Outbox. The outbox opens with the state stored in $DF_DATA_DIR/runtime/run.json. The run id in HelloAck or Assign decides whether that state is kept or discarded. Message order. A Cancel that arrives before Assign ends the run as CANCELLED without preparing the workspace. Harness files. Before the adapter starts, the runtime writes every file of Assign.harness.acp.files below /data/home, replacing what is there and creating missing directories as real directories (a symlink in their place is replaced, never followed). A path that is absolute or has a .. component fails the run before the adapter starts. The runtime writes no other harness file: the system prompt (.claude/CLAUDE.md for claude-code, .config/opencode/AGENTS.md for opencode) and Claude Code’s .claude/settings.json are files of the list. Harness environment. The harness starts with the environment of Assign (AcpHarness.env): the gateway’s inference endpoint as base URL, the placeholder API key df-placeholder and the instance CA file, or, for opencode, a configuration document in OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT and the CA in NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS; for claude-code that is ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (provider scheme claude-subscription) or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (other schemes), ANTHROPIC_MODEL (the persona’s model ID), and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (/run/factory/tls/ca.crt), plus CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 so Claude Code sends no telemetry or update checks past the endpoint. The runtime holds no model credential and reports no token usage: the gateway measures it, and usage the harness reports over ACP is not forwarded. Prompt input. The control plane releases queued messages together in one Prompts control message, in queue order, also after a reconnect. The runtime queues the whole batch before waking and starts one turn with every waiting prompt. Each message starts with its author_name and a colon, for example Peter Kurfer: or Request decision:, even for a single message. An empty name adds no author line. A continuation summary stays before the messages; hidden text blocks still reach the harness. Deploy the runtime and control plane from the same release: the old singular Prompt control message is not supported. Idle wait. After a turn that ended normally with no queued prompt (and no complete_task, rate limit, budget limit, cancel or crash), the runtime reports AWAITING_INPUT and keeps the harness session up. A Prompts batch starts the next turn in the same session (reported as RUNNING), Cancel ends the run CANCELLED, and Release or the end of the wall-clock budget ends it END_TURN. If the turn had a blocking request (a ToolCallResult with await_input_after_turn, ask_question with blocking: true), Release ends the run BLOCKED instead; the budget end still gives END_TURN. complete_task in the same turn wins and ends the run COMPLETED. The runtime has no idle timer of its own: the control plane decides when to send Release (runs.keepAliveSeconds). A lost stream does not end the wait; the runtime reconnects. Shutdown. After the final RunReport is queued, the runtime keeps trying to deliver queued messages: it flushes them over the open stream, or reconnects with the usual backoff (also when the stream drops during the flush, for example by a control plane restart), until all are acknowledged or the final report flush window of 10 minutes has passed. Messages that are not acknowledged by then stay in the outbox and a warning is logged. main waits for the connection task for the window plus 60 s for a connection attempt that is under way. Git credentials. The runtime holds no Git credentials: the gateway’s Git proxy authenticates upstream. The generated .git/config sets an empty credential.helper (resets helpers from other config scopes) and http..sslCAInfo to the instance CA, scoped to scheme://host:port/ of the workspace repo_url so other HTTPS remotes keep the system trust store; git runs with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, so a rejected request fails at once instead of prompting. credential.* and http.* entries from the repository or Workspace.git_config are dropped. Git retries. A clone, fetch or push whose output shows HTTP 503 (returned error: 503) or a connection error (Failed to connect to, Connection refused, Connection reset by peer, Empty reply from server, and mid-transfer Operation timed out, transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining, SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, Recv failure, was not closed cleanly) is retried up to 3 times. Only git’s own lines count, not remote: lines from the server. A 403 together with the gateway’s remote: df: unknown source (the gateway has no snapshot with the pod IP yet) is retried as well. Output with [remote rejected], [rejected], any other 403 or 502 (the forge rejected the proxy’s credential) is never retried, nor is any other failure (DNS errors included: the proxy host is a hostAliases entry). Before a push is retried the runtime reads the remote ref with git ls-remote; if it already has the pushed commit (the response was lost after the ref update), the push counts as successful. Lazy blob fetches of the blobless clone (during checkout) are not retried.

data: Dark Factory runs code that an AI agent writes and executes. The design assumes that the agent, the repository contents and everything the agent produces are untrusted, and puts the protection at the boundary of the sandbox instead of inside it.
data.humans#Humans: Users log in through OIDC (see Authentication); every page needs the role board-member. Sessions are server-side; the browser only holds an HTTP-only cookie. Agents cannot approve their own requests: approvals need a human, and the control plane applies the approved action itself.
data.identity#Identity:
Each sandbox pod gets its own short-lived certificate from cert-manager’s CSI driver, with the URI SAN spiffe://dark-factory/ns//pod//. The private key never lands in a Kubernetes Secret. The control plane accepts a connection only if the namespace is the sandbox namespace, the pod exists with that UID and the instance’s labels, and the connection comes from the pod’s IP, so a copied key is useless from anywhere else. The gateway identifies sandboxes by source pod IP through a registry the control plane pushes to it.
Every action of an agent is bound to its run: sandbox identity, run, task, persona and project decide which repository, branches, hosts and tools it may use.
data.known-limits#Known limits: Without Kata Containers the sandbox is a regular container on the node kernel. The egress proxy sees host names and TLS handshakes, not request contents (no TLS interception). An allowed host is allowed with every path. Network traffic that ignores the proxy settings is dropped by the NetworkPolicy and does not show in the live traffic view. Dark Factory is pre-MVP and has had no external security review.
data.principles#Principles: The sandbox is the blast radius. Inside its pod the agent may do anything. Protection covers what crosses the boundary: network traffic, Git pushes, messages to the control plane. No long-lived credentials in the sandbox. The forge credential never enters it: the Git proxy adds it on the way out, and the control plane calls the forge API itself. The model credential stays in the gateway too: the harness gets a placeholder key and the inference endpoint adds the real one. A sandbox holds no secret. Git is the only durable store for code. The task volume is a cache; the runtime regenerates the files it owns (.git/config, hooks path) before using the repository. Default deny on the network. A sandbox reaches the control plane, the gateway and nothing else unless a rule allows it. See Egress gateway. Every privileged change is audited. Egress rules, push policies, stops, cancellations, decisions on requests and every push attempt are recorded with the actor.
data.sandbox-isolation#Sandbox isolation: Layer Setting Runtime class Kata Containers microVM where configured (sandboxNamespace.runtimeClassName); without it the sandbox shares the node kernel Pod security The sandbox namespace enforces Pod Security restricted: non-root, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped Kubernetes API No service account token (automountServiceAccountToken: false); the sandbox namespace holds no Secrets Network A generated NetworkPolicy per run: egress only to the control plane agent port, the gateway and allowed cluster services; no ingress; no DNS Images The runtime and the harness are mounted as read-only image volumes; no container daemon, no nested containers
data.what-is-trusted#What is trusted: Trusted Untrusted The control plane, the gateway, the migrate job The harness and every process it starts PostgreSQL, the Kubernetes API, cert-manager The repository contents, including .git, hooks and configuration files The humans with the board-member role Everything on the task volume at the start of a run The forge, the model provider (as services, not their content) Tool output, web content and anything an agent sends to the control plane

data:
Sandboxes reach external hosts only through the gateway’s HTTPS proxy. The proxy enforces the egress rules per run and reports every connection through it to the live traffic view. Git and model traffic use their own endpoints on the gateway and do not appear there. Sandboxes resolve no DNS names themselves, which also closes DNS as an exfiltration channel.
flowchart LR S["Sandbox
HTTPS_PROXY = gateway IP"] -- "CONNECT host:443" --> P["Egress proxy"] P -- "source IP → run → rules" --> P P -- "allowed" --> H["registries, …"] P -. "denied: 403, event" .-> L["Live traffic view"] CP["Control plane"] -- "PolicyWatch: registry + rules" --> P
data.limits#Limits: No path or method rules: an allowed host is allowed completely. Tools that ignore the proxy variables cannot reach external hosts at all; their attempts are dropped by the NetworkPolicy and do not appear in the live view. The source identity relies on the CNI preserving pod IPs for in-cluster traffic.
data.live-traffic#Live traffic: Each gateway pod keeps the latest connection events in memory (nothing is persisted per event). The Network traffic page, which shows only connections through the egress proxy, merges them live from all gateway pods: a graph of sandboxes and destinations, and a table with verdicts and reasons. A not-allowlisted denial raises a network-access request on the task, so the agent’s need shows up in the inbox. How to allow or deny hosts: Network access.
data.rule-changes-reach-running-sandboxes#Rul: Rules live in PostgreSQL. A change is pushed through the control plane to every gateway pod (PolicyWatch) and applies to the next connection, typically within a second, without restarting the run. Removing a host closes the run’s open tunnels to it. The per-run NetworkPolicies are re-rendered when rules or the referenced Services change, and manual edits to them are overwritten.
data.traffic-paths#Traffic paths: Traffic Path Enforced by Agent channel Direct to the control plane agent port, mTLS NetworkPolicy HTTP(S) to external hosts Egress proxy (CONNECT or plain HTTP forwarding) Egress rules in the proxy; the NetworkPolicy lets the sandbox reach only the gateway Git Git proxy on the gateway Git proxy Model traffic Inference endpoint on the gateway, direct (not through the egress proxy) Inference endpoint In-cluster services Direct, as cluster-service rules Generated NetworkPolicy DNS Denied NetworkPolicy The pod spec sets HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY to the gateway’s ClusterIP and NO_PROXY plus hostAliases for allowed cluster services, so no name needs DNS.
data.what-the-proxy-checks#What the proxy che: Check Denial reason The source pod IP belongs to a known run unknown-source CONNECT host:port matches an allow rule of the run (exact host or *.suffix, port, default 443) not-allowlisted (403) The TLS ClientHello names the same host (SNI) sni-mismatch (tunnel closed) None of the host’s addresses is private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT or a cluster address; the proxy resolves the name itself private-destination The destination is a name, not an IP literal ip-literal Plain HTTP (GET http://…) only for rules with port 80 set explicitly denied Until a gateway pod has received its first policy snapshot it denies everything and reports not ready, so a rollout never lets traffic through unchecked. The proxy does not intercept TLS: it sees the host, the port and the TLS handshake, not paths or headers.

data:
Sandboxes clone, fetch and push only through the gateway’s Git smart-HTTP proxy. The proxy holds the forge credential, restricts what a run may push, checks every pushed commit and records every push.
flowchart LR R["Runtime / git
(sandbox)"] -- "https://gateway:8443/git/DF-12.git
no credential" --> P["Git proxy"] P -- "source IP → run → task" --> P P -- "checks, push record" --> CP["Control plane"] P -- "forge credential" --> F["Forge"]
data.allowed-ref-updates#Allowed ref updates:
A push is forwarded only if every ref update is:
Ref Allowed update refs/heads/factory/task/ create or fast-forward refs/heads/factory/wip/ create, update or delete (the WIP snapshot) Anything else (another branch, a tag, a force-push, another task’s branch) rejects the whole push before the forge is contacted. Git prints the reason, prefixed with df:.
data.credential-injection#Credential injectio:
The proxy forwards to the project’s repository URL with the project’s forge credential. It drops any Authorization header from the client, and never returns the credential to the client or writes it to a log. The runtime’s Git configuration has no credential helper, so nothing in the sandbox could hold a credential either.
http:// repositories get no route unless the instance setting network.allowPlainHttp is on; the sandbox always talks HTTPS to the gateway.
data.endpoint-and-caller#Endpoint and caller: The proxy serves https://:8443/git/.git with a certificate from the instance CA (fetch with protocol v2 and partial clone, and push). It identifies the run by the source pod IP; an unknown source, or a path naming another task than the run’s, gets 403. Until the gateway has its first policy snapshot it answers 503, which the runtime retries.
data.push-checks#Push checks:
Before forwarding, the proxy checks the commits a push adds (commits already on the forge are not checked again):
Check Finding Configurable per project Secret scan df:secret-scan: rule, path, line and a masked preview; the secret itself is never stored or logged mode approval (default) or reject Commit identity df:identity: author and committer must be the instance’s commit identity no, always enforced Protected paths df:protected-path: a change below a protected glob; .dark-factory/** is always protected globs (default CI workflow directories and CODEOWNERS) and mode Blob size df:blob-too-large: a file larger than the limit limit (default 5 MiB) and mode Linear history df:merge-commit on or off (default off) Commit limit df:push-too-large: more than 10,000 commits no Push size df:push-too-large (HTTP 413): a push body above the maximum (default 256 MiB) instance setting Pushes to the WIP branch get only the secret scan and the size limit, always rejecting.
Approval mode. A task-branch push rejected only by approval-mode findings raises a push-check-exception request in the inbox, listing the findings. Approving it creates exceptions for exactly these findings, and the agent’s next push passes them; findings in reject mode stay rejected. The agent gets a message with the masked findings either way. Board members change the modes on the project’s Push checks tab.
data.push-records#Push records:
Git traffic is not part of the Network traffic graph or the egress log, which show only connections through the egress proxy; the push records below are its trace.
Every push attempt is stored with the control plane before the client gets an answer: run, task, ref updates with old and new SHA, verdict, reasons, bytes and duration. A push is recorded as forwarding before anything reaches the forge. If the record cannot be stored within 5 seconds, the push is rejected (df:audit-unavailable).
data.upstream-failures#Upstream failures: Proxy answer Meaning 503 The forge is unreachable or timed out, or the gateway has no snapshot yet; the runtime retries 502 The forge rejected the credential (401, 403) or answered with another error; not retried Reference: Git hardening in the runtime.

data:
Harnesses reach their model provider only through the gateway’s inference endpoint. The endpoint holds the provider credential, so no model credential exists in a sandbox, and it measures the token usage of every request. The same listener serves the Git proxy.
flowchart LR H["Harness
(sandbox)"] -- "https://gateway:8443/inference/v1/messages
placeholder key" --> E["Inference endpoint"] E -- "source IP → run → model provider" --> E E -- "provider credential, streamed" --> M["Model provider"] E -- "usage records, batched" --> CP["Control plane"]
data.endpoint-and-caller#Endpoint and caller:
The endpoint serves https://:8443/inference/ with a certificate of the instance CA. The path after /inference is the path of the upstream API. It identifies the run by the source pod IP and answers 403 for an unknown source (or a run without a model provider) and 503 until the gateway has its first policy snapshot. The harness reaches it directly: the host is in the sandbox’s NO_PROXY, so the request does not use the egress proxy.
The harness gets the endpoint and a fixed placeholder key in its environment (Claude Code: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set to df-placeholder, ANTHROPIC_MODEL with the persona’s model, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS) and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1, so Claude Code sends no telemetry or update checks past the endpoint. For opencode the base URL and the placeholder key are passed inside OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT (see the agent channel reference). The placeholder is not a secret.
data.headers-and-credential#Headers and crede: The client’s Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, x-api-key, api-key, the provider’s credential header, hop-by-hop headers, Host and Content-Length are dropped; all other client headers (for example anthropic-beta) pass through. The provider’s extra headers, rendered for the run, replace client headers of the same name. The credential is set last, as the provider’s scheme defines. It is never returned to the client or written to a log. The upstream is asked for an uncompressed answer (Accept-Encoding: identity) because the usage is read from a copy of the response.
data.paths-and-status-codes#Paths and status:
Wire API Forwarded Anthropic Messages POST /v1/messages, POST /v1/messages/count_tokens, GET /v1/models OpenAI Chat Completions POST /v1/chat/completions, GET /v1/models OpenAI Responses POST /v1/responses, GET /v1/models Query strings are kept. GET /v1/models goes to the upstream of the wire API chosen for the run.
Status Reason 403 Unknown source, or the run has no model provider 404 Any other method or path, or a wire API the run’s provider does not offer; no upstream is contacted 502 The provider credential is missing from the snapshot (an unreadable Secret), the upstream URL is unusable, or the upstream cannot be connected to (connect timeout 10 s) 408 The request body from the sandbox stalled for 60 s; nothing is the provider’s fault 503 No policy snapshot yet 504 The upstream sent no response head within 10 minutes of the request starting others The upstream’s status and headers (for example 429 with retry-after) Request and response bodies are streamed as they arrive, without buffering and without a limit on the duration of a response. Unknown paths are logged at DEBUG with the path, so a missing one shows up.
data.plain-http-upstreams#Plain HTTP upstream: The provider form only accepts https upstream URLs. A stored http:// URL (for example from a database edit or an older release) is forwarded only when network.allowPlainHttp is on, like plain http:// forges; otherwise the request fails with 502 and nothing is sent. The provider credential then travels unencrypted, so use it for throwaway clusters only.
data.timeouts#Timeouts:
A model may think for minutes, so the limits are generous. They are constants, not configuration.
Limit Value When it is hit Connect (TCP and TLS) 10 s 502, usage record with unknown usage Response head 10 min after sending the request started (the upload counts) 504, usage record with unknown usage Pause in the request body from the sandbox 60 s The upload ends, 408, usage record with unknown usage Pause between two frames of the response 5 min The response ends with a stream error; the usage seen so far is recorded Streaming responses carry keep-alive events, so the pause limit only hits a stalled provider.
data.usage#Usage:
For /v1/messages, /v1/chat/completions and /v1/responses the gateway reads the model and the token counts from the final events of a stream or the usage object of a JSON body, without delaying the response. Cached input tokens are reported as cache read. A response without usage is recorded as unknown, never as zero. count_tokens and /v1/models produce no record. A request to an unreachable provider produces a record with unknown usage and no status.
The gateway reports the records to the control plane in batches (every 2 s or at 100 records), retries with backoff, buffers up to 10,000 records and then drops the oldest, counting them in df.gateway.inference.usage_dropped. The control plane stores each request once, so a retried report adds nothing twice. At most two seconds of records per replica are lost when a gateway restarts.
See Telemetry for the metrics.
data.where-the-traffic-is-visible#Where the t:
Inference traffic does not appear in the Network traffic graph or the egress log: they show only connections through the egress proxy, which is the only component that writes flow events. The same holds for Git traffic through the Git proxy, which is recorded as pushes. Model requests are visible as:
the run’s token table in the task details: one usage record per request, including requests with unknown usage; the df.gateway.inference.* metrics and, from the stored usage records, df.agent.tokens (Telemetry).

data:
Dark Factory treats agents like employees: you give them a project and a role, assign tasks, answer their questions and review their pull requests in your forge. Everything happens in the web UI; creating tasks and answering questions also works on a phone.
flowchart LR C[Credential references] --> P[Projects] C --> MP[Model providers] MP --> PE[Personas] P --> T[Tasks] PE --> T T --> R[Requests] T --> PR[Draft pull request] On a desktop screen (768 px and wider), the navigation rail on the left holds Tasks, Requests, Projects and Network traffic. The Settings link (gear) at its bottom opens the settings area with a sidebar for Personas, Credentials, Model providers and Egress rules. On a phone the settings area is not available.
Set up in this order:
Credentials, projects and personas: references to the forge and model credentials, the repositories and the agents. Model providers: the model services agents use, their models and credentials. OpenCode shows a persona with the second harness. Tasks: describe the work, follow the transcript, send messages, stop or cancel. Requests: answer questions and decide approvals. Network access: allow the hosts agents need. Delegation: agents that create tasks for other agents and wake when they end.

An artifact is a named text or image file that belongs to one task. The agent of a task writes it for you and for the tasks that are related to it: a researcher’s findings, a coordinator’s brief, a reviewer’s screenshot. Artifacts need no branch and no pull request.
data.example-research-then-decide#Example: re: sequenceDiagram participant P as DF-20 (parent) participant R as DF-22 (researcher) participant V as DF-21 (reviewer) P->>R: create_task (research the login loop) R->>R: write_artifact findings.md R-->>P: wake-up message: Artifacts: DF-22/findings.md P->>R: read_artifact (task DF-22, findings.md) V->>V: write_artifact login.png (path /tmp/login.png) V-->>P: wake-up message: Artifacts: DF-21/login.png The parent creates a research task and ends its turn. The researcher writes findings.md with write_artifact, then completes. The parent wakes with the message Artifacts: DF-22/findings.md, and reads the file with read_artifact. The key in the message is the task argument. A reviewer takes a screenshot into /tmp and attaches it with write_artifact and path. The report can show it inline: a Markdown artifact that contains ![Login](login.png) shows the image if login.png is an image artifact of the same task. Any other image reference stays a link.
data.in-the-task-view#In the task view: Artifacts tab: appears in the details once the task has an artifact, with the number of artifacts and a card each (newest first, with the first lines of a text or the image). Without artifacts the details keep the title “Details”. Transcript: a successful write_artifact shows as a row with the name and type; it opens the current version. A failed call stays an ordinary tool row. Split view (from 768 px): opening an artifact shows it next to the transcript, with the message box below the transcript. From 1280 px the details column collapses to its strip while an artifact is open; from 768 to 1279 px an open details slide-over closes. Closing the artifact restores either state. Drag the divider (or use the arrow keys on it) to change the split; the browser remembers it. Below 768 px an artifact opens on its own page. Artifact header: name, type, size and update time, for an image also its size in pixels; a Preview/Source toggle for Markdown (Source shows the highlighted text); “Open full page”; Close. Rendering: Markdown with code highlighting and Mermaid diagrams, other text highlighted by its extension, images as images. Live: when a write_artifact row arrives in the transcript, the tab and an open artifact of that name reload, and the first artifact brings the tab in without a reload. Task list: from 768 px a button collapses the task list to a strip to make room; the browser remembers the choice. Artifact page: /tasks//artifacts/ is a page of its own that you can bookmark; it does not update live. Images are served at /tasks//artifacts//raw to signed-in board members, with the stored content type, nosniff and an ETag.
data.rules#Rules: Name 1 to 100 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, ., _, -; no leading dot; case-sensitive; unique per task Content UTF-8 text without NUL bytes, or a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF image. The control plane detects the type from the content, whatever the name says. SVG and everything else is rejected Limits Text: artifacts.maxTextBytes (1 MiB). Image: artifacts.maxImageBytes (3.75 MiB) and at most 8000 px per side. Per task: artifacts.maxPerTask (50). See the configuration reference Replacing Writing an existing name replaces the artifact, also with another type. There is no history and no delete. Artifacts stay as long as the task, also when its volume is deleted A rejected write leaves an existing artifact unchanged and tells the agent which limit it hit.
data.tools#Tools:
Tool What it does write_artifact name and exactly one of content (text) or path (a file). Writes only to the caller’s own task list_artifacts Name, type, MIME type, size and update time of a task’s artifacts (task, default the caller’s) read_artifact name and optional task and offset. Text comes in pages of at most 64 KiB, with a first line that names the byte range and the offset of the next page; an image comes as an image path is read by the runtime in the sandbox: it is absolute, lies under /data/repo or /tmp, passes through no symlink and names a regular file of at most 8 MiB. Anything else fails the call.
An agent can read the artifacts of its own task, its ancestors, its descendants (all levels) and the tasks it depends on (depends_on). Any other task, and a task that does not exist, gives the same error “task not found or not related”. What an agent reads from another task is marked as data written by another agent; reads of other tasks are recorded in the audit log with the target task and the artifact.

data: An agent can hand work to other personas: it creates tasks, lets them wait for each other and is woken when they end. This guide shows the pattern “implementation and review”. It needs no forge webhook; webhooks add the merge of a pull request as a signal (Forge webhooks).
data.dependencies#Dependencies:
depends_on is a list of {task, kind}. It is set when the task is created and never changes. All targets must be tasks of the same project.
Kind Satisfied when the target completion has completed at least once (the agent called complete_task and the run ended; not if it was cancelled meanwhile), or is done done is done: its pull request was merged, or a board member marked it done A satisfied dependency stays satisfied. A task with an unsatisfied dependency starts as awaiting_dependencies: no run, branch, volume or sandbox. When the last dependency is satisfied it becomes queued and starts like any task. Dependencies gate only the first start: a later completion of the target does not restart a task that has run. A message queued on a waiting task does not start it; the first run receives it with the assignment.
Marking a task done by hand satisfies done dependencies on it, also without webhooks. Cancelling a waiting task discards its assignment.
data.example-implementation-review-and-the-ne: sequenceDiagram participant H as You participant C as Coordinator DG-1 participant I as Implementation DG-2 participant R as Review DG-3 H->>C: create the task C->>I: create_task C->>R: create_task (depends_on DG-2, completion) Note over R: awaiting_dependencies I->>I: complete_task I-->>C: wake: DG-2 completed I-->>R: released, starts R->>R: complete_task R-->>C: wake: DG-3 completed, findings C->>I: send_message: address the findings I->>I: complete_task I-->>C: wake: DG-2 completed Describe the work to the coordinator persona. It calls list_personas, then create_task for the implementation and for the review with depends_on: [{task: "DG-2", kind: "completion"}], and ends its turn. The review shows awaiting dependencies.
