The implementation completes. The review is released in the same transaction and the coordinator is woken. The review completes with findings and wakes the coordinator, which relays them with send_message to the implementation. The message reopens it. The implementation completes again and wakes the coordinator; if the coordinator wants another review round it sends a message to the review task, which a completion dependency does not start again. Later rounds are the coordinator’s job. Without webhooks, done dependencies are released by marking the target done in its status menu. With webhooks a merged pull request does it.
data.in-the-task-view#In the task view: The details of a task show Created by and Parent after the branch, and a collapsible Dependencies section between the properties and the runs: Waits for (each dependency with its kind and whether it is satisfied) and Needed by (the tasks that wait for this one, with their status). It is open while the task awaits its dependencies and updates live. The section is absent for a task in no dependency.
data.limits#Limits: There is no limit yet on the depth of the task tree, the number of children or relayed messages; watch the transcript and cancel a task that runs away. A persona is not restricted in whom it may delegate to.
data.the-parent-wakes-when-a-child-ends#The p:
When a child completes, becomes done, fails or is cancelled, its parent gets a message in the same moment. A parent that is done, cancelled or failed gets none; neither does a parent for a child that waits for a human.
DG-3 "Greeting review" completed. PR: https://forge.example/acme/app/pulls/12 Artifacts: DG-3/findings.md Still waiting on DG-3: DG-4 Summary from the agent of DG-3: > Review done, two findings. The text names the key and title of the child and how it ended (completed, is done, failed with its reason, was cancelled), the pull request if there is one, the child’s artifacts as / (Artifacts: none if it has none; those of its own children are not listed), the tasks that still wait for the child, and the child’s own summary, quoted. The summary is the child’s output: the parent treats it like any untrusted text. The message is authored by the system with the reason task.child_ended.
A child that completes and later has its pull request merged wakes the parent twice, once for each. A child that is already done wakes the parent no second time when a run of it completes. A run that ends completed on a cancelled child counts as nothing: no completion, no released dependents, no message.
data.the-tools#The tools:
Every task of an agent gets three more factory tools:
Tool What it does list_personas Returns the name and the description of every persona, ordered by name. create_task Creates a task in the project of the caller with persona, title, prompt and optional depends_on. The caller becomes the parent. Returns the key and the status of the new task. send_message Queues a message on a child of the caller, with the same effect as your message in the task view. The caller cannot message any other task. Tasks created in the UI have no parent. A task created by an agent shows that agent as its creator in the details.

data:
A model provider is the model service a persona works with, together with the one credential Dark Factory uses for it. Agents never hold that credential: their harness talks to the gateway’s inference endpoint with a placeholder key, and the gateway adds the real credential on the way out. The gateway also reads the token usage of every request, so the run card shows the same numbers for every harness.
Dark Factory passes three wire APIs through unchanged and does not translate between them:
Wire API Paths the gateway forwards Anthropic Messages POST /v1/messages, POST /v1/messages/count_tokens, GET /v1/models OpenAI Chat Completions POST /v1/chat/completions, GET /v1/models OpenAI Responses POST /v1/responses, GET /v1/models Routing features (fallback between providers, load balancing, GitHub Copilot subscriptions) are not part of Dark Factory. Use an LLM router such as agentgateway and configure it as the upstream URL of a model provider.
data.create-a-provider#Create a provider:
Settings → Model providers → New model provider. The dialog has two tabs: General (the form below) and Models (the model list). A preset prefills both; it is not stored, the provider keeps the values you save. Every change is audited.
Field Required Meaning Name, Preset yes, no Name is unique and shown on the persona form. Preset (only when creating) prefills the form. Wire APIs and upstream URLs at least one Each offered API with the base URL of the upstream. The URL uses https and has no user info, query or fragment. A base path is kept: https://host/inference/go/openai receives /v1/chat/completions as https://host/inference/go/openai/v1/chat/completions. Credential reference, Credential scheme yes The credential reference names the Secret key that holds the provider’s key or token; the page shows the reference, never the value. The scheme says how the gateway presents the credential, see below. Header, Value Header: scheme Custom header; prefix: no A preview of what the gateway sends: the header name, then the prefix and an example token (sk-…example…4f7a, a fixed text, not your key). Both are disabled when the scheme fixes them: x-api-key for scheme x-api-key, Authorization with prefix Bearer (with the space) for bearer and claude-subscription. With Custom header you set the header and an optional prefix, for example api-key without prefix or Authorization with Token . The name may be any valid header name except hop-by-hop headers, Host and Content-Length. Extra headers no One Name: value per line, see below. Disabled for the Claude subscription scheme, and a save with extra headers for it is rejected. Changing the scheme updates the Header and Value preview; the form keeps its size and what you typed in Header, Value and Extra headers, also while the scheme disables them. A save stores only what the scheme uses.
data.credential-schemes#Credential schemes: Scheme Header sent to the upstream x-api-key x-api-key: bearer Authorization: Bearer header : claude-subscription Authorization: Bearer ; Anthropic Messages only, only for personas with the harness claude-code, and no extra headers The client credentials (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, x-api-key, api-key, and the header of the scheme) are removed from every request before the gateway adds its own.
data.extra-headers#Extra headers:
The value of an extra header is a template over task_id, task_key, run_id, project_key and persona_id, with one filter, sha256 (lowercase hex). The control plane renders it once per run; it replaces a header of the same name that the harness sends.
x-opencode-session: {{ task_id | sha256 }} All runs of a task send the same value, so the provider can group them as one session. The form rejects unknown filters and variables, and names the problem. Extra headers cannot be named like a credential header (Authorization, x-api-key, api-key, the header of the scheme), a hop-by-hop header, Host or Content-Length: the gateway owns these.
data.models#Models:
The tab Models lists the models personas of this provider can select. A model has:
Field Required Meaning Model ID yes The ID the upstream expects in the model field, unique within the provider. Wire API yes The API the model is served over. A model uses one API; if the upstream serves it over two, add it twice under different IDs. The select lists all three APIs, but the save is refused for an API the General tab does not offer (“gpt-6-luna uses OpenAI Responses, which this provider does not offer (tab General).”). Context, Max output both or neither Context window and maximum output in tokens, positive whole numbers. OpenCode uses them to track the context and to compact it; without them it assumes none. + Add model appends a row, the trash button removes one. The list is not stored in the order you typed it: after saving it is sorted by model ID. Problems show under the row (a limit without the other, a model ID twice, an API the provider does not offer) and on the list (a removed model that a persona uses: “minimax-m3 cannot be removed: persona Ada uses it.”). A removed wire API that a model still uses is refused as well.
data.persona-and-harness#Persona and harness:
A persona uses exactly one model provider and one model of it. Each harness can use some wire APIs:
Harness Wire APIs claude-code Anthropic Messages opencode OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages The persona form lists only providers that offer a wire API of the harness, and below them the models of the chosen provider whose wire API the harness can use. The model is required. Changing the harness or the provider updates the lists and drops a choice that no longer fits. A claude-subscription provider is only offered to claude-code.
A run uses the wire API of its persona’s model. The control plane gives the harness the gateway URL, the placeholder key df-placeholder and the instance CA, in environment variables or, for opencode, in a generated configuration (see Run a persona with OpenCode). Claude Code gets the persona’s model through ANTHROPIC_MODEL; its small and fast model is not set.
A provider cannot be deleted while a persona uses it, a model cannot be removed while a persona uses it, and a change of scheme or of a model’s wire API that a persona’s harness cannot use is refused. The messages name the personas.
data.presets#Presets:
Preset Wire APIs and upstream Scheme Anthropic Anthropic Messages, https://api.anthropic.com x-api-key Claude subscription Anthropic Messages, https://api.anthropic.com claude-subscription OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses, https://api.openai.com bearer OpenCode Go Chat Completions and Responses, https://opencode.ai/inference/go/openai; Anthropic Messages, https://opencode.ai/inference/go/anthropic; header `x-opencode-session: {{ task_id sha256 }}` Presets prefill models too (context window and max output as in OpenCode’s catalog):
Preset Models Anthropic, Claude subscription claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5 on Anthropic Messages (1000000 / 128000) OpenAI gpt-6-luna, gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra on Responses (1050000 / 128000) OpenCode Go Chat Completions: glm-5.3 (1000000 / 131072), kimi-k3 (1048576 / 131072), deepseek-v4-pro (1000000 / 384000); Anthropic Messages: minimax-m3, qwen3.8-max (1000000 / 131072), claude-haiku-5-5 (1000000 / 128000); Responses: gpt-6-luna (1050000 / 128000) The lists age with the services; change them in the form before you save (remove a model, add claude-opus-5-6), and edit the provider later to add new ones.
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting: Symptom Cause The model provider is missing on the persona form The provider offers no wire API of the harness, or uses claude-subscription with another harness. The model select of the persona form is empty The provider has no model on a wire API of the harness: add one on the provider’s Models tab. Requests answer 502 model provider credential unavailable The Secret of the credential reference cannot be read: check the reference, the Secret and the key. Gateways pick up a rotated Secret within a minute. Requests answer 502 model provider unreachable The gateway cannot connect to the upstream URL. The run card shows “N requests without usage” The provider’s responses carried no usage (for example an OpenAI stream without include_usage).
data.use-a-claude-subscription#Use a Claude s:
kubectl -n dark-factory create secret generic claude-token --from-file=token= with a token from claude setup-token. Settings → Credentials → New credential reference: name claude, the Secret claude-token, key token. Settings → Model providers → New model provider, preset Claude subscription (header, value and extra headers are disabled: the scheme fixes them), name it, choose the credential reference, save. Settings → Personas → New persona: harness claude-code, model provider the one you created, a model of it (for example claude-sonnet-5-5). api.anthropic.com does not have to be on the egress allowlist: model traffic goes to the gateway, which connects to the provider itself. That traffic is not shown in the network graph; see where the traffic is visible.
Claude Code would also send non-essential traffic (telemetry, update checks) directly, not through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Dark Factory sets CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 for Claude Code, so this traffic does not appear in the network graph.
data.use-an-openai-compatible-provider#Use an: Create the credential reference for the API key. New model provider, preset OpenAI (or empty), set the URL of your service, scheme bearer. Add the models of the service on the Models tab (the preset has the usual ones). A persona with the harness opencode can select any of them; claude-code only models on Anthropic Messages.
data.use-opencode-go#Use OpenCode Go: Create the credential reference for the OpenCode Go key. New model provider, preset OpenCode Go; the session header is already filled in. The preset has the models of Go with the API each is served over. claude-code personas can select the ones on Anthropic Messages, opencode personas all of them: see Run a persona with OpenCode.

data: A sandbox reaches no external host until a rule allows it (see Egress gateway). Board members manage the rules on the Egress rules page and watch the traffic on the Network traffic page.
data.allow-a-host-an-agent-needs#Allow a host:
When an agent hits a blocked host, the gateway reports it and a network-access request appears in the Requests inbox, with the host and port. Three ways to allow it:
From the request: approve it and pick the scope (task, project or everywhere). The agent gets the decision as a message; its retry succeeds. From the traffic view: on a blocked row or graph node choose Allow, then the scope. On the Egress rules page (Settings → Egress rules): New egress rule, host, port and scope. Any new host rule settles the pending requests it covers.
data.kinds-of-rules#Kinds of rules: Rule Allows Scopes Host (http-host) CONNECT to a host name (registry.npmjs.org) or all subdomains (*.npmjs.org) on one port (default 443; 80 only when set) instance (“Everywhere”), project, task Cluster service (cluster-service) direct connections to a Kubernetes Service, for example a build cache; reachable by its DNS name without DNS (hostAliases) instance, project Deny rule nothing; it silences requests for a host that should never be allowed (below) instance A run may use the union of the instance rules, its project’s rules and its task’s rules. A new rule applies to the next connection of running sandboxes within about a second; no restart needed. Cluster services must be in a namespace the chart allows (clusterTargets).
data.network-traffic-page#Network traffic pag: The page shows live connections through the egress proxy from all gateway pods (model requests and Git traffic use their own endpoints and are not listed; see where the traffic is visible): a graph of sandboxes and destinations on the left (blocked edges dashed red), the events on the right, newest first. Filter by domain or IP, by verdict (All, Blocked, Allowed) and under Advanced by persona, sandbox, project or task. Pause stops the stream. A row’s details show what the gateway records: method, status, duration, bytes, SNI, source, gateway pod, the reason and the matching rule. Request contents inside TLS are not inspected. Events live in memory only; a restarted gateway pod starts empty.
data.silence-a-host-that-should-never-be-allo:
Some harnesses send telemetry to hosts you will never allow (for example Claude Code to http-intake.logs.us5.datadoghq.com:443). Every run raises the same request for it. A deny rule ends that:
Open Settings → Egress rules and choose New egress rule. Select Deny. “Applies to” and Port are disabled: a deny rule covers every project and every port. Enter the host (http-intake.logs.us5.datadoghq.com, or *.datadoghq.com for all subdomains) and choose Add deny rule. Shortcuts: Deny always on a network-access request in the inbox (denies the request and creates a rule for its exact host) and Deny always on a blocked row of the network traffic page.
What a deny rule does:
Case Result A run connects to the host Still blocked (not-allowlisted). The gateway is unchanged. The gateway reports the denial No request is raised. An agent asks for the host (request_approval) The agent gets “denied by instance policy” and nothing is stored. Pending requests for matching hosts exist They are denied on creation, as the system principal, with a comment naming the rule. An allow rule for the host exists The allow rule still wins: the deny rule only silences requests. Traffic page Matching rows show “Deny rule” and offer no actions. Open pages pick up a new rule when the stream reconnects. Deleting the rule makes the host raise requests again. Creating and deleting are audited as egress_deny_rule.create and egress_deny_rule.delete.

data: OpenCode is the second harness next to Claude Code. It speaks ACP (opencode acp) and works with any model provider that serves a model over OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses or Anthropic Messages, so a persona is not tied to one vendor. Like every harness it reaches its model only through the gateway’s inference endpoint with a placeholder key.
data.create-the-persona#Create the persona: Create the credential reference for the provider’s key (Credentials). Settings → Model providers → New model provider, for example with the preset OpenCode Go. On the Models tab check the models and their wire APIs; add the ones you need. Settings → Personas → New persona: harness opencode, the model provider, and a model of it, for example glm-5.3. The provider list shows only providers that offer a wire API of OpenCode, the model list only models served over one. A provider with the scheme claude-subscription is not offered: it is for claude-code. Create a task for the persona. The first run starts OpenCode from the harness image (harness.opencode.image).
data.repository-configuration#Repository conf:
OpenCode reads the opencode.json and the .opencode/ directory of the repository. This stays in effect:
agents, commands and custom tools of the repository; MCP servers (remote ones are subject to the egress policy); permissions, except the two tools below; the repository’s AGENTS.md, including nested ones. The generated configuration is merged last and always overrides:
model, the title model and small_model: they stay the persona’s model; the providers that may be used: only df; plugins: denied; the question and websearch tools: denied, even when the repository allows them. A provider that the repository defines stays configured but unused, and OpenCode contacts its host when it starts. If the egress policy denies that host, OpenCode does not start and the run fails at the start of the harness; the denied request shows in the egress log. Remove the provider from the repository’s opencode.json or allow its host.
The reference table is in Agent channel configuration; the keys harness.opencode.image, .adapterCommand and .env of the instance configuration (chart values image.harness.opencode.*) change the image, command and environment.
data.session-resume#Session resume: OpenCode keeps its session state below HOME (/data/home), which is on the task volume. The next run of the task starts with the harness session id of the previous run and loads the session, so OpenCode continues with its conversation. If it cannot, the run starts a new session and the control plane passes a summary of the earlier runs, as for Claude Code.
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting: Symptom Cause The run fails right at the start and names the harness harness.opencode.image is blank and the project sets no adapter command. The run fails at the start of the harness and the egress log shows a denied host The repository’s opencode.json defines a provider with that host. Remove the provider or allow the host. Model requests answer 502 See Model providers. Reasoning output of a model looks plain OpenCode’s catalog marks models with a field that carries reasoning text; a model of a Dark Factory provider has no such entry, so only the display of reasoning is affected.
data.what-a-run-gets#What a run gets:
The control plane generates OpenCode’s configuration for every run and passes it in the environment, so it ranks above the user’s and the repository’s OpenCode configuration:
One provider df that points at /inference/v1 with the placeholder key, and your model as model and small_model. The AI SDK package follows the wire API of the model. The model’s context window and max output tokens are passed when the model has them; OpenCode uses them to track the context and to compact it. Update checks and the model catalog download are off. OpenCode contacts no host besides the gateway unless a tool needs one or the repository’s opencode.json defines a provider (see Repository configuration). The persona’s system prompt is OpenCode’s global AGENTS.md. The repository’s own AGENTS.md still applies: project configuration stays enabled, so the model sees both.
data.what-is-disabled-and-why#What is disable: Feature State Why question tool denied A blocking question ends the turn of a run. Agents ask humans with the factory tool ask_question, which fits that model. websearch tool denied There is no search provider behind it. Plugins denied A plugin in the repository’s or a global configuration would be installed from a package registry, which the sandbox cannot reach, and would run code in the harness. webfetch tool allowed It goes through the egress proxy like every other outbound request: allow the host in Network access. MCP servers of the repository allowed Remote servers fail at the egress policy unless the host is allowed and only log warnings. The factory MCP server is always available.

data:
Agents ask before they guess, and they cannot grant themselves anything. Both show up as requests: in the Requests inbox (the count is on every page) and as cards on the task’s timeline.
Kind Raised by You decide Question the agent, with up to 5 suggested answers tap a suggested answer or write one network-access approval the gateway when a host is blocked, or the agent with a reason approve for the task, the project or everywhere; deny; or Deny always (Network access) push-check-exception approval the Git proxy when a push hits findings in approval mode approve exactly these findings for this task, or deny (Git proxy)
data.blocking-and-non-blocking#Blocking and n: A blocking question stops the agent’s work until it is answered. If nobody answers within the idle deadline, the run ends and the task becomes blocked; your answer later queues the task again and the next run continues with it. A non-blocking request lets the agent carry on, for example with a fallback.
data.what-happens-on-a-decision#What happens:
The control plane applies an approved action itself (it creates the egress rule or the push exception); the agent never does. The decision reaches the agent as a message at its next turn, including your comment. Identical pending requests of a task are merged; a task can have at most 20 pending requests. Completing or cancelling a task closes its pending requests. Raising, deciding and closing are audited. The request card on the task timeline keeps the answer or approval outcome and who decided it. The decision message is hidden in the transcript and queued-message stack, so the answer does not appear a second time. Its full content still reaches the agent.
For prompt diagnostics, an operator can enable web.showHiddenBlocks (optional, default false; instance configuration). Hidden decision messages then appear labeled Instruction for the agent, with the author Request decision.
Request texts (questions and approval reasons) come from the agent and are rendered as Markdown with the same rules as agent messages: HTML in the text is shown as text, images appear as links, unsafe links are dropped, fenced code is highlighted and mermaid fences are drawn as diagrams in an isolated frame.

data: Everything below is configured in the web UI by a board member and stored in the database. Every create and edit is audited with the old and new values.
data.credential-references#Credential referen:
Dark Factory never stores secret values. A credential reference names a Kubernetes Secret in the instance namespace and a key in it; the control plane reads the value when it uses it.
Create the Secret, for example kubectl -n dark-factory create secret generic claude-token --from-file=token=. Settings → Credentials → New credential reference: a name, the Secret name and the key. Two kinds of credentials are referenced:
Credential Used by Reaches the sandbox Forge credential (a token of a bot account) the forge plugins (API) and the Git proxy never Model credential (for example a Claude subscription token or an API key), referenced by a model provider the gateway’s inference endpoint never; the harness gets a placeholder
data.personas#Personas:
A persona is an agent with a role. Settings → Personas → New persona:
Field Meaning Name Shown in the task list and transcript, for example “Linus”. Description Optional, at most 500 characters: the role and strengths of the persona. The persona card shows it, and agents read it through list_personas when they choose whom to delegate to. System prompt The role and the working rules of this agent. Harness The coding agent that runs in the sandbox: claude-code or opencode (guide). Model provider The model provider the harness talks to. Only providers that offer a wire API of the harness are listed. Model Required. One of the models of the provider whose wire API the harness can use. Changing the harness or the model provider updates the other selects. A persona has no adapter command; a project can set one (Projects).
Every task is assigned to one persona; the persona’s harness, model and prompt apply to all runs of the task.
data.projects#Projects:
Projects → New project:
Field Meaning Name, Key Display name and the task key prefix (DF → tasks DF-1, DF-2, …). The key is 2–10 capital letters or digits, starting with a letter, and cannot change later. Repository URL HTTPS clone URL. Its host selects the forge plugin; the hint below the field names it. Base branch Where task branches start and pull requests point to. Issue tracker URL Optional. Sandbox image The image the agent works in. It needs git and a shell; the runtime and the harness are mounted into it. Adapter command Optional. Replaces the instance’s harness image for this project (a harness installed in the sandbox image). Forge credential The credential reference for the forge. Wake tasks on reviews and mentions Whose PR reviews and @mentions of the bot account wake a task when forge webhooks are set up: Nobody, Members with write access (default) or Anyone. Merged or closed pull requests and failed checks apply regardless. The Push checks tab sets what the Git proxy checks for this project: protected paths, secret scan and blob size, each in mode approval or reject, and whether merge commits are allowed.
Users with the role admin also see the tab Lifecycle events: the instance public key and the project’s lifecycle event subscriptions. Subscriptions save on their own; Save project does not apply to them.
The project list shows the number of queued, running, waiting and done tasks per project.

data: A task is a piece of work for one persona in one project. Its code lives on the branch factory/task/; the agent opens a draft pull request with its first commit and you review it in your forge.
data.agent-messages-markdown-code-and-diagram:
An agent message is plain text while it streams and is rendered as Markdown when its turn ends.
Safety: the text is untrusted. HTML in it is shown as text, images appear as links (the browser loads nothing an agent names), links with unsafe schemes are dropped and every link opens with rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow". Code: a fenced block is highlighted when its info string names a language or file extension (```rust, ```rs). Blocks without a language, with an unknown one or over 64 KiB stay plain; the language is never guessed from the content. The theme follows the browser’s light or dark color scheme; the operator picks the themes with web.codeTheme.light and web.codeTheme.dark (instance configuration). Diagrams: a ```mermaid fence is drawn as a diagram in the browser, in a light or dark theme following the color scheme. The diagram runs isolated from the page (sandboxed iframe), so its source cannot run script in the page. A diagram that cannot be parsed stays a code block with a one-line error. The diagram renderer (about 3 MB) is loaded only on pages that contain a diagram. Without JavaScript the diagram source is shown as a code block.
data.create-a-task#Create a task: New task (the green button) opens the composer: pick the project, describe the work, pick the persona and send. The task gets the next key of the project (DF-12) and starts as soon as a run slot is free. Without a title, the first sentence of the description is used until the agent sets a better one; you can rename a task at any time.
data.follow-and-steer-it#Follow and steer it:
The task view has three columns: the task list, the transcript and the details.
Transcript: the agent’s messages and tool calls (commands, file reads and edits) live, as they happen. Forge activity appears in between: pushes to the task branch (with the commit range, or the reason if the push was rejected), and the pull request being opened and marked ready, with a link to it. These rows come from the control plane and the gateway, not from the agent, and are never sent to the agent. Messages: type into the message box at any time. A message reaches the agent at the next turn boundary, without restarting anything; while it waits it is shown as queued and can be edited or removed. A message to a finished task reopens it. A message to a task that awaits its dependencies is delivered in its first run. Details: what the agent is doing now, the pull request and issue links, project, persona, branch, who created the task and its parent (for a task an agent created), the dependencies and the list of runs with model and token usage. The tokens are summed per model from the gateway’s usage records; requests whose response carried no usage are counted separately (“2 requests without usage”) instead of as zero. Artifacts: once the agent has written an artifact, the details get an Artifacts tab with a card per artifact; an artifact opens next to the transcript. The transcript shows the author of each message. In the queued-message stack, messages from agents and the system are prefixed with their name; your own messages have none. System authors use readable names instead of internal reason codes: Task assignment, Resume, Request decision, Push check, Forge events and Subtask update. Other system authors show Dark Factory. Request decisions appear on their cards; their delivery messages are hidden by default.
data.status#Status: Status Meaning awaiting_dependencies Created with an unsatisfied dependency; it has no run, branch or sandbox and becomes queued when the last dependency is satisfied queued Work is pending; a run starts when a slot is free or the resume time has passed running A run is working on it waiting The agent finished its turn and waits for you; the sandbox stays alive for a while (runs.keepAliveSeconds) blocked A blocking question or approval was not answered in time; answering resumes the task in_review The agent called complete_task; the pull request is ready for review rate_limited The model provider’s usage limit was hit; the task resumes automatically at the shown time limit_reached A budget of the run, or the harness’s token or turn limit, was reached; a message continues it completed Marked done by a human, or its pull request was merged cancelled Cancelled by a human failed The run failed and automatic retries are exhausted The list’s filters group them: Active, Waiting (awaiting_dependencies, waiting, blocked, in_review, limit_reached) and Done (completed, failed).
data.stop-mark-done-cancel#Stop, mark done, c:
From the status menu in the details:
Action Effect Stop (also the stop button in the message box) Ends the current run; the agent finalizes (pushes, snapshots) and the task waits for your next message. Mark done The task becomes completed and its pull request is marked ready for review (a background job, retried if the forge is down). Cancel task Stops the run, discards queued messages and closes pending requests. The pull request stays as it is. A new message reopens the task. Reset workspace Deletes the task’s volume (not possible while a run is active). Committed work and the WIP snapshot stay in Git; the next run clones again. All of them are audited with your name.
data.where-the-work-is#Where the work is: Where What factory/task/ Commits of the agent, pushed after every turn factory/wip/ Snapshot of uncommitted files at the end of each run (secrets such as .env and keys excluded) Draft pull request Opened on the first commit ahead of the base branch; marked ready when the task completes. Forge failures are retried for an hour Task volume Cache of the checkout between runs; deleted 7 days after the task closed or after 30 days without a run
